observations.statement: Rectangular pool; inner dimensions 69.2 by 45.5 m. North W1, east W2, south W3, west W4; central island B102.
observations.phase: source attributed Herodian; exact construction date at an aperture unknown

observations.basis: explicit excavation-access gap versus source synthesis
observations.statement: Excavators did not discover the entrance of water or the connection to the Urtas channel. Source later attributes aqueduct supply to the lower complex.

Only three soundings reached pool floor. B5 west-wall face masked by probably Byzantine wall; upper W4 displaced east c.0.25m. B31 exposes original floor and south W3 face with continuous rounded hydraulic plaster. B3/B12 establish east-wall stepped base/fill; none is a surveyed inlet.
observations.phase: local original fabric plus later masking/disturbance; no inlet contact

observations.statement: Ill11 restored schematic section and Ill47 proposed tholos reconstruction; neither is an observed inlet section.

observations.basis: observed pool, excavator function interpretation, source-defined placement
observations.statement: Pool 3.6 by 2.0m and 2.0m deep, six steps; interpreted as frigidarium in Roman bath in central block of northern wing. This wing lies north of main pool complex.
observations.phase: source included in Herodian northern-wing ensemble; pool-specific sealed construction date not supplied

observations.statement: Pool 3.5 by 1.4m and 2.7m deep south of C11/2; only western edge excavated to floor, with c.0.40m of broken Herodian vessels.
observations.supply: nearby covered channel may have fed both pools; continuation missing

observations.statement: Incoming storage-hall channel enters 1.1 by 1.1m pool, probably settling tank; two channels leave. Bottom not reached at 2m. System probably original Herodian phase.

observations.feature: Service-building B58 small pool and B40/B58 channel
observations.basis: observed channel entry and construction over destroyed hall; uncertain chronology
observations.statement: Covered channel enters 1.3 by 1.0m pool. Both built on thick fill above destroyed original B52 floor (+658.45m). Urtas connection inferred; nearest known aqueduct segment c.200m northwest. Source leaves event synchronization with service-hall rebuilding uncertain.
observations.underlying_surface: B52 original floor at +658.45m as source gives
observations.phase: later than B52 hall; exact synchronous link to service reconstruction unknown

observations.statement: Eastern-plateau fill assigned to original Herodian construction. Service pottery subdivided into lower-floor and later upper-floor/dump contexts. Synthesis proposes overall construction 23–15 BCE; no B101 inlet construction date is supplied.

exploratory_audit.source_site_complex: Greater Herodium (B101, northern-wing bath pools and service-building pools in same source)

code_basis.conduit: permissive source-attributed supply rule; NOT an observed B101 aperture
code_basis.great: large/main pool, p28/p53; exceeds published smaller-pool dimensions
code_basis.northern: C11/2 and C35 in northern wing north of B101, pp46–48/52

exploratory_audit.strict_same_phase_limit: Small pools and great-pool observed use/construction contacts not proven contemporaneous; B58 explicitly later. Lane-level source-complex relative position is not a full phase-controlled test.
